solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Japanese verse reporting shrill sound made by dove?

indicators.note: reporting means the phrase that follows is spoken, so we want its sound

parts.note: a dove's noise is a coo, and a shrill one is a high coo

explanation.surface: A poem seemingly describing the piercing call of a dove.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the classic three-line Japanese poetic form of seventeen syllables.

clue.text: He's swallowing a novel hospital drug

indicators.note: the letters of he's take in the following pieces

parts.note: taken as letters, the apostrophe dropped
She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A man is ingesting a new hospital medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new' but is a book title: SHE, Haggard's adventure story.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of hashish, the cannabis resin, which is a drug.

clue.text: Bungling agent held up by one immediately following

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the synonym for agent is held inside the word for immediately following

parts.note: next means immediately following

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep, or representative, is a sales agent

explanation.surface: An incompetent spy is delayed by somebody right behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unskilled who bungles a task is clumsy and lacking expertise.

clue.text: Innocent, but lacking capacity to cover special case

indicators.note: the word for lacking capacity surrounds and covers the special case

parts.note: unable means lacking capacity
an exception is a special case

explanation.surface: Someone innocent who could not cope with an exceptional case.
explanation.definitionFit: Inoffensive and beyond reproach, so nothing can be objected to: blameless or harmless.

clue.text: His kind goes around gaping

indicators.note: the synonym of kind encircles the word his, which sits inside it

parts.note: a kind person is decent

explanation.surface: Someone's type of person apparently wanders about with mouth open.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for seed pods or fruit that burst open, so it describes something split and gaping.

clue.text: Figures perhaps slightly raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the phrase is turned upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a tad means slightly

explanation.surface: Numbers, maybe, that went up a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures such as statistics are one example of information collected; 'perhaps' marks this.

clue.text: On radio, learn of storm primarily in this area

indicators.note: radio is heard, so this signals a word chosen for how it is said

parts.note: to learn of something is to hear it
about means concerning, of

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of storm

explanation.surface: A broadcast tells listeners about a storm in their area.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning near here or in this vicinity.

clue.text: Firm in Monaco quietly replaced Arab fellow?

parts.note: firm means stable, steady

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in a different place

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A company in Monaco quietly swapped one Arab colleague for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' reads as a person but is a horse breed: an Arab's fellow is another horse in the same yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse trained in the same yard as another is its companion there, so one horse's fellow.

clue.text: Object songbird found in English city

indicators.note: the bird is found inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York city
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A thing, a bird, is discovered in an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: An object is any distinct thing that exists, a synonym in the philosophical sense.

clue.text: Most of the people in ancient Balkan country

indicators.note: most of means one letter of the word the is dropped

parts.note: a people is a race

explanation.surface: The majority of a population lived in an old Balkan land.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient region of south-east Europe, now split between Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.

clue.text: Southern Europeans put off trapping a bird, perhaps

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: the synonym of put off holds the letter a within it

parts.note: to put off is to deter

explanation.surface: People from southern Europe are discouraged when they catch a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird such as a finch that lives on seeds is an example; 'perhaps' flags that birds are only one kind.

clue.text: Trying to get hold of beams endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the synonym of beams loses its first and final letters

parts.note: roof beams are rafters

explanation.surface: Someone straining to grab the roof timbers that seem to go on forever.
explanation.definitionFit: To be after something is to be seeking or chasing it, as in 'the police are after him'.

clue.text: Anticipate former teacher's favourite touring clubs

parts.note: ex is a prefix meaning former

indicators.note: the word for the teacher's favourite goes round the abbreviation for clubs

parts.note: the favourite pupil is the teacher's pet
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Looking ahead to a former teacher's best-loved pupil going round golf or night clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something is to look for it to happen; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Graceful fleet regularly observed in sea

indicators.note: the picked letters are seen inside the name of the sea

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea in northern Europe

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of fleet is taken

explanation.surface: A navy moving elegantly, sighted at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Something like ballet dancing is elegant and graceful in movement.

clue.text: More sensible to engage one's orthopaedic auxiliary

indicators.note: the comparative word takes on, enclosing, the possessive

parts.note: better means more sensible, wiser
taken as letters, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Wiser to hire someone's assistant in an orthopaedic department.
explanation.definitionFit: An unqualified practitioner who sets broken limbs works as a helper to fracture medicine.

clue.text: Bacteria? Poetic sort sadly harbours hundreds

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the two hundreds inside
sadly suggests the words poetic sort are in a poor state, rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A melancholy poet type seems to be sheltering hundreds of germs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges POETIC SORT into STREPTOCOI, and 'harbours' puts CC within it. The question mark admits the definition names a class by its group.
explanation.definitionFit: These round bacteria form chains and cause infections such as strep throat.

clue.text: Forebear caught stabbing a wise old king

indicators.note: the abbreviation for caught pierces the name of the king

parts.note: Nestor was the wise old king of Pylos in Homer
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An ancestor arrested while knifing an aged monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is someone from whom one is descended, a synonym.

clue.text: Company runs hotel in pleasant coastal road

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: the letter for hotel goes inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: pleasant means nice
Hotel is H in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A firm runs a hotel on an agreeable seafront drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A road cut along a cliff face by the sea, like those on the Riviera.

clue.text: Music in motet Verdi revised?

indicators.note: revised means the letters of in motet Verdi are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A query about music in a sacred choral piece reworked by Verdi.
explanation.definitionFit: A light instrumental composition in several movements, as written by Mozart, is a kind of music.

clue.text: Jam Scottish girl left unfinished on ship

indicators.note: the girl's name is left without its end letter

parts.note: Morag is a Scottish girl's name
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A Highland lass abandons her preserves aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam is a tricky situation one is stuck in, like a bog one is mired in; both mean a predicament.

clue.text: Spirit finally haunting wide Russian river

indicators.note: finally takes the last letters of haunting and wide

parts.note: the Neva flows through St Petersburg

explanation.surface: A ghost at last haunting a broad river in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for gin, from Dutch jenever, which is a spirit.

clue.text: European river engulfing slender shrub

indicators.note: the river's name swallows the synonym for slender

parts.note: the Oder flows between Germany and Poland
slender means lean

explanation.surface: A river in Europe swamping a thin bush.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen flowering bush, poisonous and common in Mediterranean gardens, is an example of a shrub.

clue.text: A minister recalled in Tennessee lodging-place

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: TN is the postal abbreviation for Tennessee

indicators.note: recalled means the abbreviation for a minister is called back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A clergyman remembered while staying somewhere in Tennessee.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn or pub, historically offering beds to travellers, is a place to lodge.

clue.text: Sticky substance overrunning a Pacific island

indicators.note: the sticky substance spreads over and around the letter a

parts.note: gum is a sticky substance

explanation.surface: Glue spilling over an island in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: A US territory in Micronesia, in the western Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Bitter as a native of Belgrade, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase tells us to take what is said aloud, not what is written

parts.note: someone born in Belgrade, Serbia's capital, is a Serb

explanation.surface: Someone from Serbia's capital described as sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rarer variant of acerbic, meaning sharp or sour in taste or temper.

clue.text: I sit out in court abandoned like some holidays

indicators.note: the jumbled pair of words goes inside the other jumble
abandoned suggests the word court has been let loose and scrambled
out means the letters of I sit are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone sits outside while a court is deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate jumbles: 'abandoned' scrambles the court, 'out' scrambles I SIT, and 'in' nests the second inside the first, just before its final C.
explanation.definitionFit: Package holidays aimed at sightseers are tourist-oriented, which describes some trips.

clue.text: Producer of rolls finally invests in a famous racehorse

indicators.note: finally takes the last letters of the words invests and in

parts.note: Red Rum won the Grand National, Britain's great steeplechase, three times in the 1970s

explanation.surface: Someone at last puts money into a celebrated horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' suggests bread or Rolls-Royces; here it is drum rolls. Red Rum is the most famous British racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A military percussion instrument with wires across its base produces the rattling drum roll.

clue.text: Railwaymen once given points to look after

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a former British trade union
S and E are compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Old railway workers are told how to care for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend or care for someone, such as a sick person, is to look after them.
